title: Scottish graveyard that is 'world's most haunted' where ghost attacks visitors
excerpt: It also has a unique connection to Harry Potter.
content:
It also has a unique connection to Harry Potter.

19:01, 24 Oct 2026

Halloween is the best time of year for ghost stories, and with October 31 less than a week away now is the perfect opportunity to delve into the history of one of Scotland's most infamous graveyards. Not only is it considered to be potentially the most haunted graveyard in the world, but one of the spirits that allegedly calls it home has earned a reputation for attacking visitors.

‌

‌

Greyfriars Kirkyard is the graveyard that surrounds the 17th century Greyfriars Kirk parish church in Edinburgh, situated along the southern edge of the Scottish capital's Old Town. There have been burials held at the site for hundreds of years, including dozens of famous Edinburgh locals.

‌

Among the most famous residents said to have been buried at the kirkyard is Greyfriars Bobby, with a headstone commemorating the loyal dog situated at the entrance to the graveyard. You can also find a statue of the beloved Terrier a short walk away, which is unsurprisingly a popular tourist spot.

If you are a Harry Potter fan, you might know that Greyfriars Kirkyard has very important ties to the children's fantasy series. Graves around the kirkyard are thought to have inspired various Harry Potter characters, and you will indeed find gravestones for Robert Potter, William McGonagall, Thomas Riddell, and more around the grounds.

‌

The Category A listed site is also closely tied to the history of the Covenanters, with more than 1,000 members of the 17th century religious and political movement reportedly imprisoned in a field near the kirkyard. Years later, when this area was integrated into the graveyard as vaulted tombs, it became known as the Covenanters' Prison.

The most infamous spirit said to roam Greyfriars Kirkyard is the Mackenzie Poltergeist, who according to legend haunts a tomb that is known as the Black Mausoleum. Not only does this malicious ghost allegedly wander the graveyard, but he has even supposedly attacked visitors in the past.

‌

Locals believe that the Mackenzie Poltergeist is the spirit of George Mackenzie, who was a Lord Advocate of Scotland in the late 17th century who persecuted Covenanters and is said to have tortured and executed hundreds of them. Unsurprisingly, before his death in 1691, he earned the nickname of 'Bloody Mackenzie'.

‌

According to Edinburgh supernatural experts City of the Dead Tours, there have been hundreds of alleged attacks since 1999 that have been attributed to the Mackenzie Poltergeist. Many of these encounters have been rather brutal in nature, with some visitors reportedly leaving with nasty injuries.

‌

City of the Dead Tours states: "Attacks include scratches, cuts, bruises, burns and bites on witnesses’ bodies—often under their clothes. Many people collapse or are knocked over. There are hot and cold spots. Cameras and watches stop working. There have been unexplained smells and auditory anomalies—including knocking noises under the ground and inside the tomb itself.

"Dead animals are found, unmarked, in front of the Black Mausoleum. People have complained that an unseen apparition has pulled their hair, grabbed their legs and arms or hit them."

Not only has the site reportedly been unsuccessfully exorcised twice, but there have even been reports of paranormal activity in the houses surrounding the kirkyard. Whether any of this is actually true will probably never be proven, but you can head to Greyfriars Kirkyard yourself this Halloween to learn more if you are brave enough.
